issues.detail: Error handling is thin: no guidance on API failures such as 4xx/5xx or rate limits, retries, or batch sends over 1,000 recipients, and the in-memory seenTokens set has no expiry or multi-instance handling beyond a comment.

scenarios.name: eu-batch-newsletter-with-variables
scenarios.rationale: Both satisfy all rubric points (api username, MAILGUN_API_KEY, EU url, domain as first arg, JSON.stringify'd recipient-variables keyed by email, %recipient.x% placeholders); B additionally puts the first name in the subject and explicitly notes the domain-vs-From argument, while A's use of form-data is also correct but slightly less explicit on the domain point.

scenarios.name: secure-webhook-handler-bounces
scenarios.rationale: A meets all rubric points, including returning 401 on failure, while B returns 406 for invalid signatures (violating the 401 requirement) and silently returns 200 on a replayed token instead of rejecting it, though B's signature check, timestamp window, and event handling are otherwise correct.

scenarios.name: inbound-support-route-and-validation
scenarios.rationale: B uses mg.routes.create with match_recipient and forward()/stop(), notes the MX requirement, uses mg.validate.get with check.result and risk, and flags validation as separately metered, while A uses raw curl instead of the SDK calls, omits the metering/plan caveat (it only mentions a validation-enabled plan), and doesn't use mg.validate.get.
